entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This appeal is directed against the order dated 23.11.2020 passed in S.B. Civil Writ Petition No.12202/2020, wherein the writ petition filed by the appellants/writ-petitioners, has been dismissed.

2. The writ-petitioners filed the writ petition aggrieved of the notification dated 18.10.2019 (Annex.1) issued by the Sub Divisional Officer, Bhopalgarh, District Jodhpur for acquisition of the land for the purpose of construction of the State Highway No.86-C.

Submissions were made that the acquisition was being made contrary to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re- Settlement Act, 2013 (Act of 2013) and the Rules made thereunder.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re- Settlement Act, 2013 (Act of 2013)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. During the course of hearing before the learned Single Judge, it was noticed that questioning the action of the respondents, a civil suit was filed by the writ-petitioners before the Civil Judge, Pipar City, District Jodhpur wherein, an injunction was granted to the writ-petitioners, wherein the authorities were directed not to dispossess the writ-petitioners without proceeding in accordance with law.

entities.text: Civil Judge, Pipar City, District Jodhpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Court also noticed that after passing of the said injunction order, the Land Acquisition Officer-cum- S.D.O., Bhopalgarh issued a notice to the writ-petitioners under Section 21 of the Act of 2013 on 05.10.2020 requiring the writ- petitioners to submit their explanation alongwith claim in respect [2023:RJ-JD:38602-DB] (3 of 4) [SAW-100/2021] of 0.0069 hectare of land in Khasra No.938/27 of village Bhopalgarh.

Based on the fact that suit was pending, wherein injunction was granted, and the authorities under the Act of 2013 were seized of the matter, the Court didn't find any reason to interfere under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and dismissed the writ petition.

4. Counsel for the appellants made submissions that despite the fact that the writ-petitioners, in response to the notice under Section 21 of the Act of 2013, have responded by way of raising objection, inter-alia, qua the nature of the land in question, as the land has been indicated as 'Bara',
whereas the same is commercially converted land, the authority under the Act of 2013 has not decided the same and, therefore, merely on account of pendency of the proceedings before the authority, the petition couldn't have been dismissed.
5. We have considered the submissions made by the counsel for the appellants and have perused the material available on record.

6. The grievance, as raised by the appellants regarding nature of the land the quantum of compensation, likely to be determined and paid to the writ-petitioners, admittedly is pending consideration before the Land Acquisition Authorities.

The fact that the notice was issued on 05.10.2020 and the writ-petitioners have responded to the same and the same hasn't been decided so far, cannot be a reason enough to interfere with the order of the learned Single Judge.

: RJ-JD:38602-DB] (4 of 4) [SAW-100/2021] expeditiously, preferably within a period of four weeks from the date a copy of this order is placed by the appellants/writ- petitioners with the said authority.
8. Qua the orders, to be passed by the authorities, the writ- petitioners would be free to take appropriate proceedings in accordance with the provisions of the Act of 2013.
9. With the above observations and directions, the appeal stands disposed of.
